## Overview

**EarthCARE** (Earth Cloud, Aerosol and Radiation Explorer) is a joint ESA/JAXA
satellite mission launched in May 2024.  It carries four co-aligned instruments
— a Cloud Profiling Radar (CPR), an Atmospheric LiDAR (ATLID), a Multi-Spectral
Imager (MSI), and a Broad-Band Radiometer (BBR) — designed to characterise
clouds, aerosols, and their radiative effects.

The S3 bucket at `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/EarthCARE/` holds two
product types:

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Satellite | EarthCARE |
| Agency | ESA / JAXA |
| Orbit type | Sun-synchronous, ~97 min period |
| Swath type | Nadir-pointing curtain (along-track) |
| Data format | HDF5 (`.h5`) |
| S3 bucket | `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/EarthCARE/` |
| Products available | `AC__CLP` (cloud profiling), `AUX_MET` (geolocation/met grid) |
| Date range in bucket | 2026-01-24 – 2026-02-18 |
| Total granules (each product) | 142 |

---

## S3 bucket organisation

Files are arranged under two product prefixes, each following a
`{PRODUCT}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/` hierarchy:

```
s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/EarthCARE/
  AC__CLP/
    2026/
      01/
        24/   ← 6 granules
        25/   ← 5 granules
        …
      02/
        18/   ← last available day
  AUX_MET/
    2026/
      01/
        24/   ← 6 granules (same orbit segments as AC__CLP)
        …
      02/
        18/
```

Each day typically contains 5–6 granule files per product, corresponding to
the orbit segments that pass over the region during that UTC day.  Both product
types are co-timed: each `AC__CLP` granule has a matching `AUX_MET` granule for
the same orbit segment and time window (identified by the shared orbit number
and sensing-time stamp in the filename).

### `AC__CLP` — L2B Combined Cloud Profiling

Product code `AC__CLP_2BS`.  Combines CPR and ATLID retrievals to produce
vertical profiles of cloud and precipitation properties at 1 km and 10 km
along-track resolution.  File size ~28–36 MB per granule.

### `AUX_MET` — Auxiliary Meteorological / Geolocation Grid

Product code `AUX_MET` (file type `AUX_JSG_1DS`).  Provides the co-located
geolocation grid (latitude, longitude, altitude) and meteorological context
fields (temperature, humidity, pressure) resampled onto the EarthCARE
along-track × across-track standard grid.  File size ~33 MB per granule.

---

## File naming convention

Both product types follow the same ESA Earth Explorer filename template:

```
ECA_{sensor}_{product_type}_{sensing_start}_{sensing_stop}_{orbit_id}{direction}_{version}.h5
```

### `AC__CLP` example

```
ECA_J_AC__CLP_2BS_20260124T0354_20260124T0406_09417B_vCa.h5
```

| Field | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ECA` | — | EarthCARE mission prefix |
| `J` | `J` | Joint instrument product (CPR + ATLID) |
| `AC__CLP_2BS` | — | Product type: combined cloud profiling, L2B swath |
| `20260124T0354` | — | Sensing start: 2026-01-24 03:54 UTC |
| `20260124T0406` | — | Sensing stop: 2026-01-24 04:06 UTC |
| `09417` | — | Absolute orbit number |
| `B` | `B` / `D` | Orbit direction: `B` = ascending, `D` = descending |
| `vCa` | — | Product version |

### `AUX_MET` example

```
ECA_E_AUX_JSG_1DS_20260124T0354_20260124T0406_09417B_vBc.h5
```

| Field | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `E` | `E` | Spacecraft-level product (ECMWF-collocated) |
| `AUX_JSG_1DS` | — | Auxiliary Joint Standard Grid, 1D swath |
| remaining fields | — | Same convention as `AC__CLP` above |

---

## File contents

Both products use the same top-level HDF5 structure:

```
/
├── HeaderData/
│   ├── FixedProductHeader/     ← mission, file type, version strings
│   └── VariableProductHeader/
│       ├── MainProductHeader/  ← orbit metadata (orbit number, sensing times,
│       │                          frame lat/lon, state vectors)
│       └── SpecificProductHeader/
└── ScienceData/                ← geophysical and geolocation arrays
```

### `AC__CLP` — `ScienceData` contents

#### `ScienceData/Geo/` — geolocation

| Dataset | Shape | dtype | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | `(nalong,)` | float64 | Footprint latitude (degrees) |
| `longitude` | `(nalong,)` | float64 | Footprint longitude (degrees) |
| `height` | `(nalong, nheight)` | float32 | Altitude of each range bin (m) |
| `surface_elevation` | `(nalong,)` | float32 | Surface elevation (m) |
| `time` | `(nalong,)` | float64 | Seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00:00 UTC |
| `Scan_Time/*` | `(nalong,)` | int/float | Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, MilliSecond |
| `day_night_flag` | `(nalong,)` | int8 | 0 = day, 1 = night |
| `land_water_flag` | `(nalong,)` | int8 | Surface type flag |

A typical granule spans ~4 945 along-track footprints × 206 range-height bins
(1 km resolution).

#### `ScienceData/Data/` — cloud/precipitation retrievals

Variables come in pairs at two resolutions: `_1km` (full resolution,
~4 945 × 206) and `_10km` (averaged, same along-track count × 206 bins).
Selected key variables:

| Dataset | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cloud_radar_reflectivity_1km` | dBZ | Attenuated radar reflectivity factor |
| `cloud_extinction_1km` | /m | Cloud extinction coefficient |
| `cloud_backscatter_1km` | /m/sr | Cloud backscatter coefficient |
| `cloud_doppler_velocity_1km` | m/s | Cloud Doppler velocity |
| `attenuated_backscatter_1km` | /m/sr | Total attenuated backscatter |
| `cloud_water_content_1km` | kg/m³ | Cloud liquid water content |
| `cloud_ice_content_1km` | kg/m³ | Cloud ice water content |
| `cloud_effective_radius1_1km` | μm | Cloud effective particle radius |
| `cloud_particle_category_cpr_atlid_1km` | — | Particle category flag |
| `cloud_mask_cpr_atlid_1km` | — | Combined CPR/ATLID cloud mask |
| `quality_flag_1km` | — | Per-bin quality flags `(nalong, nbins, 10)` |
| `optical_thickness_1km` | — | Column cloud optical thickness `(nalong,)` |
| `cloud_water_path_1km` | kg/m² | Column cloud water path `(nalong,)` |

Fill value: `9.969209968386869e+36` (IEEE 754 special value).

### `AUX_MET` — `ScienceData` contents

| Dataset | Shape | dtype | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float64 | 2D grid latitude |
| `longitude` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float64 | 2D grid longitude |
| `altitude` | `(nalong, nheight)` | float32 | Altitude levels (m) |
| `height` | `(nheight,)` | float32 | Standard height levels |
| `surface_elevation` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float32 | Surface elevation (m) |
| `time` | `(nalong,)` | float64 | Along-track time |
| `land_flag` | `(nalong, nacross)` | int8 | Land/water mask |
| `sensor_altitude` | `(nalong,)` | float32 | Spacecraft altitude |
| `sensor_azimuth_angle` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float32 | Viewing azimuth |
| `sensor_elevation_angle` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float32 | Viewing elevation |
| `solar_azimuth_angle` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float32 | Solar azimuth |
| `solar_elevation_angle` | `(nalong, nacross)` | float32 | Solar elevation |

A typical `AUX_MET` granule has dimensions ~5 145 along-track × 207 across-track
× 242 height levels.

---

## Creating a VirtualZarr IceChunk store

The following demonstrates building an IceChunk store that holds virtual
references to three consecutive `AC__CLP` granules directly from their S3 URLs.
No data is downloaded; only chunk byte-range metadata is written to the store.

The store merges variables from both `ScienceData/Geo` (geolocation) and
`ScienceData/Data` (retrievals) into a single dataset.  The along-track
dimension is given the name `nalong` and a decoded `datetime64` coordinate
(`time`) is attached so that `.sel(time=...)` works.  The height-bin dimension
is named `nheight` and left as an integer index.

### Setup

```{python}
import os
os.environ.setdefault("RUST_LOG", "error")

import io
import h5py
import icechunk
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
import obstore
from obstore.store import S3Store
from obspec_utils.registry import ObjectStoreRegistry
from virtualizarr.parsers import HDFParser
from virtualizarr.writers.icechunk import virtual_dataset_to_icechunk
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
```

```{python}
S3_BUCKET = "airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket"
S3_PREFIX = "JOIN/EarthCARE/AC__CLP"
S3_REGION = "us-west-2"

# Three consecutive granules from 2026-01-24 (orbit 09417–09419, ascending)
GRANULES = [
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2026/01/24/ECA_J_AC__CLP_2BS_20260124T0354_20260124T0406_09417B_vCa.h5",
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2026/01/24/ECA_J_AC__CLP_2BS_20260124T0526_20260124T0538_09418B_vCa.h5",
    f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{S3_PREFIX}/2026/01/24/ECA_J_AC__CLP_2BS_20260124T0659_20260124T0711_09419B_vCa.h5",
]

STORE_DIR = Path("../_data/earthcare/icechunk-stores/ac_clp_demo").resolve()

# EarthCARE time epoch (TAI seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00:00 UTC)
EC_EPOCH = np.datetime64("2000-01-01T00:00:00", "ns")
```

### Helper: read coordinates from a granule

Coordinates (time, latitude, longitude) are small 1-D arrays (~5 000 values).
We read them eagerly — one `obstore.get` call per granule — and use them as
loadable dimension coordinates in the final dataset.

```{python}
s3_store = S3Store.from_url(f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/", region=S3_REGION)
registry = ObjectStoreRegistry({f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/": s3_store})


def read_ec_coords(url: str) -> dict:
    """Read time, latitude, longitude arrays from an AC__CLP granule."""
    key = url.removeprefix(f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/")
    buf = io.BytesIO(obstore.get(s3_store, key).bytes())
    with h5py.File(buf, "r") as f:
        time_sec = f["ScienceData/Geo/time"][:]   # float64, seconds since EC_EPOCH
        lat      = f["ScienceData/Geo/latitude"][:]
        lon      = f["ScienceData/Geo/longitude"][:]
    time_ns = (time_sec * 1e9).astype("int64")
    time_dt = EC_EPOCH + time_ns.astype("timedelta64[ns]")
    return {"time": time_dt, "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon}
```

### Open virtual datasets and attach coordinates

We open two virtual datasets per granule (`ScienceData/Geo` and
`ScienceData/Data`), rename the generic `phony_dim_*` axes to `nalong` and
`nheight`, merge them into one dataset, then attach the loadable coordinate
arrays.

```{python}
geo_parser  = HDFParser(group="ScienceData/Geo")
data_parser = HDFParser(group="ScienceData/Data")

# EarthCARE uses -9999 as a secondary missing-data sentinel (meaning "no
# retrieval / no cloud detected") in addition to the declared _FillValue of
# 9.96921e+36.  Adding missing_value=-9999 to each float variable's attrs
# ensures xarray's mask_and_scale=True masks both sentinels.
EC_MISSING = -9999.0

def add_missing_value(vds):
    """Add missing_value attr to all float variables that lack it."""
    new_vars = {}
    for name, var in vds.data_vars.items():
        if var.dtype.kind == "f" and "missing_value" not in var.attrs:
            new_attrs = dict(var.attrs) | {"missing_value": EC_MISSING}
            new_vars[name] = var.assign_attrs(new_attrs)
    return vds.assign(new_vars)


vds_list = []
for url in GRANULES:
    # --- virtual datasets (no data downloaded) ---
    vds_geo  = geo_parser(url,  registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()
    vds_data = data_parser(url, registry=registry).to_virtual_dataset()

    # Rename phony dims to meaningful names.
    vds_geo  = vds_geo.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nalong", "phony_dim_1": "nheight"})
    vds_data = vds_data.rename({"phony_dim_0": "nalong", "phony_dim_1": "nheight",
                                 "phony_dim_2": "nqflag"})

    # Merge both groups into one dataset and annotate missing values
    vds = add_missing_value(xr.merge([vds_geo, vds_data]))

    # --- loadable coordinates (small, downloaded now) ---
    coords = read_ec_coords(url)
    vds = vds.assign_coords(
        time      =("nalong", coords["time"],
                    {"long_name": "observation time", "timezone": "UTC"}),
        latitude  =("nalong", coords["latitude"],
                    {"long_name": "latitude",  "units": "degrees_north"}),
        longitude =("nalong", coords["longitude"],
                    {"long_name": "longitude", "units": "degrees_east"}),
    ).set_index(nalong="time")

    vds_list.append(vds)
    print(f"  {url.split('/')[-1]}: nalong={vds.sizes['nalong']}, nheight={vds.sizes['nheight']}")
```

### Write to an IceChunk store (append per granule)

VirtualiZarr's `virtual_dataset_to_icechunk` accepts an `append_dim` argument
that resizes the store and appends new virtual chunk references — no data is
moved.  We write the first granule normally, then append the remaining two
along `nalong`.

```{python}
shutil.rmtree(STORE_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
STORE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

config = icechunk.RepositoryConfig.default()
config.set_virtual_chunk_container(
    icechunk.VirtualChunkContainer(
        f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/", icechunk.s3_store(region=S3_REGION)
    )
)
repo = icechunk.Repository.create(
    icechunk.local_filesystem_storage(str(STORE_DIR)), config=config
)

for i, (url, vds) in enumerate(zip(GRANULES, vds_list)):
    session = repo.writable_session("main")
    if i == 0:
        virtual_dataset_to_icechunk(vds, session.store)
    else:
        virtual_dataset_to_icechunk(vds, session.store, append_dim="nalong")
    session.commit(f"Append granule {i}: {url.split('/')[-1]}")
    print(f"  committed granule {i}")

print(f"Store written to {STORE_DIR}")
```

### Re-open and inspect

```{python}
repo2    = icechunk.Repository.open(
    icechunk.local_filesystem_storage(str(STORE_DIR)),
    authorize_virtual_chunk_access={f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/": None},
)
ds = xr.open_zarr(
    repo2.readonly_session("main").store,
    consolidated=False,
    mask_and_scale=True,   # masks both _FillValue (9.96921e+36) and missing_value (-9999)
)
print(ds)
```

The `nalong` dimension is indexed by `datetime64` time values, enabling
time-based selection with `.sel()`:

```{python}
# Select a 10-minute window by time
window = ds.sel(nalong=slice("2026-01-24T04:00", "2026-01-24T04:10"))
print(f"Footprints in window: {window.sizes['nalong']}")
print(window[["latitude", "longitude", "cloud_radar_reflectivity_1km"]])
```

## Visualizations

### Vertical curtain: radar reflectivity

The radar reflectivity curtain shows the vertical structure of clouds along
the satellite track.  We load a short segment from the middle of the combined
three-granule swath.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)

FILL = 9.969209968386869e+36

# 30-minute segment from orbit 09418
seg = ds.sel(nalong=slice("2026-01-24T05:26", "2026-01-24T05:56"))
refl = seg["cloud_radar_reflectivity_1km"].values          # (nalong, nheight)
lat  = seg["latitude"].values

# Fill values are already NaN (mask_and_scale=True); clip any residuals
refl = np.where(np.isfinite(refl), refl, np.nan)

# Height axis: EarthCARE bins run top-down (bin 0 ≈ 20 km, bin 205 ≈ −0.5 km).
# Passing height values in descending order means pcolormesh naturally places
# high altitude at the top — no invert_yaxis needed.
nheight = refl.shape[1]
height_km = np.linspace(20, -0.5, nheight)   # approximate; exact in ScienceData/Geo/height

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 4))
pcm = ax.pcolormesh(
    lat, height_km, refl.T,
    cmap="RdYlBu_r", vmin=-30, vmax=20, shading="auto"
)
plt.colorbar(pcm, ax=ax, label="Radar reflectivity (dBZ)", pad=0.01)
ax.set_xlabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_ylabel("Altitude (km)")
ax.set_title("EarthCARE AC__CLP — Attenuated Radar Reflectivity (1 km)\n"
             "Orbit 09418 · 2026-01-24 · ascending pass")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Vertical curtain: cloud extinction (ATLID)

```{python}
ext = seg["cloud_extinction_1km"].values
ext = np.where(np.isfinite(ext), ext, np.nan)
# Clip extreme values for display
ext_clipped = np.clip(ext, 0, 0.05)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 4))
pcm = ax.pcolormesh(
    lat, height_km, ext_clipped.T,
    cmap="plasma", vmin=0, vmax=0.03, shading="auto"
)
plt.colorbar(pcm, ax=ax, label="Cloud extinction (/m)", pad=0.01)
ax.set_xlabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_ylabel("Altitude (km)")
ax.set_title("EarthCARE AC__CLP — Cloud Extinction Coefficient (1 km)\n"
             "Orbit 09418 · 2026-01-24 · ascending pass")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Column-integrated cloud optical thickness

```{python}
ot  = seg["optical_thickness_1km"].values
ot  = np.where(np.isfinite(ot), ot, np.nan)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 3))
ax.plot(lat, ot, color="steelblue", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Latitude (°N)")
ax.set_ylabel("Optical thickness")
ax.set_title("EarthCARE AC__CLP — Column Cloud Optical Thickness\n"
             "Orbit 09418 · 2026-01-24")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
